items.title: Outback city's first new hotel in decades being manufactured 4,600km away
paras: Rita Brooks on site for the first concrete pour for the new Kalgoorlie Airport Hotel. ( ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas )
Construction of a new $40 million hotel for Kalgoorlie-Boulder in regional Western Australia is progressing in Penang, Malaysia.
Modular building techniques are becoming more popular amid shortages of skilled tradespeople, particularly in regional areas.
The 165-room Kalgoorlie Airport Hotel is scheduled to open in the middle of next year.

An assembly line in Malaysia is a world away from Australia's biggest outback city, but a Swedish-owned modular building company is slowly piecing together the components for a new four-star hotel in regional Western Australia.
Amid construction cost blowouts and ongoing shortages of skilled tradespeople, the development of Kalgoorlie-Boulder's first new hotel in decades is shining a light on modular building techniques.
While proponents say it could speed up delivery projects across regional Australia, significant challenges within the construction sector remain.
The concrete foundations for the $40 million Kalgoorlie Airport Hotel were poured this month.
Rita Brooks and her son Jason Brooks on site for the pouring of the concrete foundations. ( ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas )
The new hotel is the brainchild of Perth businesswoman Rita Brooks, whose family has owned The View on Hannans Motel in Kalgoorlie-Boulder since it was built in the 90s.

Ms Brooks bought the vacant land for the new hotel in 1996. Spent years searching for a builder, eventually engaging Stockholm-based firm SIBS after spotting an advertisement promoting its modular designs during a visit to the Malaysian capital, Kuala Lumpur.
She subsequently toured the company's factory in Penang, where 90 modules for the hotel are currently under construction.
Construction is underway on the Kalgoorlie Airport Hotel at a factory in Penang, Malaysia. ( Supplied: Rita Brooks )
The modules are to be shipped in late December from Malaysia to Fremantle and trucked nearly 600 kilometres to Kalgoorlie-Boulder, where installation will require a 300-tonne crane.
"This is the first design they've done for Australia, so it's a learning curve for them (SIBS) as far as reaching Australian compliance, which has taken about 18 months," Ms Brooks said.
"Every item has had to meet Australian standards and that in itself was a challenge, so that's probably why a lot of people haven't gone and done this path."
SIBS has since struck a deal with Singaporean-headquartered Centurion Corporation to supply modules for a seven-storey, 302-room hotel development in Port Hedland in WA's Pilbara.
Jason Brooks on a tour of the SIBS factory in Malaysia. ( Supplied: Rita Brooks )
Master Builders Western Australia has estimated the state will be short more than 10,000 key construction workers by 2030 without action to rebuild the industry's workforce.
It says the cost of building a new house in WA has more than doubled since the pandemic, increasing by 105.4 per cent, while building material inflation has recently accelerated to a three-year high.
WA Deputy Premier Rita Saffioti (left) and Matt Moran (middle) touring an under-construction home. ( ABC News: Keane Bourke )
Master Builders WA chief executive Matt Moran said the increasing popularity of modular construction was due to skills shortages.
"With ongoing labour pressures, work is moving into factories to keep up with demand … this form of construction offers a high level of control over quality, safety and speed," he said.
Matt Moran speaks at a press conference on a construction site in Sinagra earlier this year. ( ABC News: Keane Bourke )
"With modular, there are generally short site time frames where manufacturing for standard-type layouts can take weeks, with installation typically completed in days," he said.
"In regional and remote areas where transport and site preparation can be expensive … it can be complex, which does require careful planning and coordination.
"These challenges facing regional and remote WA show that modular construction can be in some cases a viable solution."
The proposed development has been reduced from four storeys to three due to escalating costs. ( ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas )
The modular method has received significant state-level support, with the Cook government announcing a $49 million package in May to help 15 manufacturers move into modular construction.

But the sector's difficulties were underlined by the collapse of Welshpool-based Offsite (Maneon Pty Ltd), which manufactured prefabricated timber building components until it entered administration in October, with creditors seeking to recoup $41 million.
The Kalgoorlie Airport Hotel project has faced its own cost challenges since the state government's Regional Development Assessment Panel approval in 2024.
The original budget was $20 million but has doubled to $40 million, while the number of rooms has been reduced from 200 to 165.
Ms Brooks said the overruns meant she had seriously considered walking away from the project.
But it is scheduled to open next year and will be the mining city's first new hotel development since the Kalgoorlie Rydges Hotel was built in the early 2000s.
The proposed Kalgoorlie Airport Hotel development has been reduced in scale from 200 rooms to 165. ( ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas )
It also arrives amid a crippling shortage of available hotel rooms amid the city's latest mining boom.
"For regional Western Australia, this type of building system is unique but will be embraced, I believe, going forward because it answers a lot of questions," Ms Brooks said.
"We want a quality build, and we want it within a year; we don't want to wait three years.
Rita Brooks and her site manager watch the concrete foundations being poured. ( ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas )
But Ms Brooks also expressed frustration at being unable to secure state and federal government support for her project, specifically for the installation of infrastructure like power and water.
"The private investor is taking 100 per cent of the risk, but 100 per cent of the benefit will be that we have a new housing system for regional Australia which can work," she said.
"If this system can be used, and if it can get government support, they will be the winners."

items.title: Doctors report missing out on paid parental leave and job offers while pregnant
paras: Some doctors claim they have experienced discrimination after falling pregnant. ( AP Photo: LM Otero, file )
A trainee doctor claims New South Wales Health retracted her job offer months after she revealed she was pregnant.
She is among several doctors who have spoken up following a Four Corners investigation into pregnancy discrimination.
NSW Health says it does not comment on individual cases, but takes "any allegations of pregnancy or parental leave discrimination seriously".
A trainee doctor claims New South Wales Health discriminated against her when it retracted her job offer months after she revealed she was pregnant.
She is among several doctors across Australia who have told Four Corners they believe they were penalised for having children while pursuing a career in medicine.
Alice, who wished to keep her surname private, was pregnant when she was offered a three-year training position as a doctor in the NSW Ministry of Health.
"I was under no legal obligation to disclose my pregnancy status, but I did after accepting my position," she told Four Corners.
Months before her proposed start date, however, Alice said she received a phone call informing her that her employment offer had been withdrawn.
"[The decision] was so unbelievably bad … that I almost didn't think it would actually ever eventuate," Alice said.
With similar training positions in NSW already filled, Alice faced the prospect of moving interstate or delaying her specialty training.
After escalating the matter with the NSW Ministry of Health and seeking legal advice, Alice was eventually offered the position again.
But she said NSW Health offered her a two-year contract rather than the three years she had initially been offered.
"The whole experience has put a really sour taste in my mouth," Alice said.
A NSW Health spokesperson said the department was unable to discuss individual employment matters publicly, but said it took "allegations of pregnancy or parental leave discrimination seriously".
"NSW Health recruitment processes are required to be merit-based, fair and lawful," the spokesperson said in a statement.
"Pregnancy and parental leave should not disadvantage a person in recruitment or employment."
A Four Corners investigation found pregnancy discrimination was still occurring across Australia, revealing it could happen regardless of industry, seniority, pay or where you lived.
Scores of women have since come forward with their own allegations, including many in the medical field.
Intensive care specialist Behny Samadi has spent more than a decade working for NSW Health and is on maternity leave from St George Hospital.
Instead of receiving her regular private patient billing income at Level 4 during her 14 weeks of paid parental leave, Dr Samadi claims she was pushed down to Level 1.
Behny Samadi says her pay has been cut by about 20 per cent during paid parental leave. ( Supplied: ASMOF NSW )
"I feel utterly betrayed … by the system that allowed it to happen," she said.
"I really do love the public service and I find so much value in what we do. I don't want to leave, but it's stuff like this that makes it really, really hard to stay."

A NSW Health spokesperson said the department did not determine a staff specialist's rights of private practice level, but "any concerns raised by staff are taken seriously and considered through the appropriate processes".
"NSW Health also provides parental leave entitlements to eligible employees in accordance with applicable employment arrangements and policies," the spokesperson said in a statement.
Imogen Hines, an emergency medicine registrar at a regional NSW hospital, said a lack of job security in medicine often disadvantaged pregnant women indirectly.
"Having to apply for a job every 12 months meant that I knew somebody would not hire me if they knew I was going to be off for a few months on parental leave," she said.
Imogen Hines says she hid her pregnancy over fear of being unemployed. ( Supplied: Imogen Hines )
Dr Hines said the rigid structure of surgical training programs meant she effectively had to choose between her dream specialty or starting a family.
She abandoned her plans to become an orthopaedic surgeon and switched to emergency medicine in 2025.
"It's the frequent rotations, the late notice of where you're going to be working and the lack of permanent contracts," Dr Hines said.
"All of these things make you really vulnerable and make it really difficult to plan around having a family."
Imogen Hines says a career in orthopaedics was incompatible with raising a family. ( Supplied: Imogen Hines )

Australian Medical Association (AMA) Tasmania branch president Meg Creely said she was "overwhelmed" by the number of doctors who contacted her following Four Corners's investigation into pregnancy discrimination .
"A lot of people talked about if they disclosed a pregnancy — no matter what legal ramifications there are — suddenly they weren't getting that role for the next year," she said.

Dr Creely said Tasmanian doctors were hit particularly hard by strict rules governing access to paid parental leave, because they often lost their entitlements by moving interstate to progress their training.
Meg Creely says Tasmanian doctors have reported experiencing pregnancy discrimination. ( Supplied: AMA Tasmania )

A Tasmanian health department spokesperson said it "acknowledged that doctors undertaking accredited specialist training programs can face unique challenges due to the rotational nature of their training, including moving between health services and jurisdictions as part of training requirements".

"The department and the AMA have also been discussing options to accommodate the specific needs of Tasmanian doctors, who are required to move between employers or jurisdictions as part of their training, to see how this can be accommodated so that they are not disadvantaged," the spokesperson said.

In October, Four Corners reported exclusively on a report by Sex Discrimination Commissioner Anna Cody, which called for an overhaul of laws to stop workplaces "penalising" pregnant women and mothers.
The federal government has not yet committed to implementing the report's recommendations.

"The Sex Discrimination Act 1984 makes it unlawful to discriminate on these grounds in certain areas of public life, such as employment," a spokesman for Attorney-General Michelle Rowland told Four Corners.
"The government thanks the Sex Discrimination Commissioner for her report, which the government is carefully considering."

items.title: ASX set for gains, global stocks rise; Oil prices climb
paras: Advertisement Business Markets World markets ASX set for gains, global stocks rise; Oil prices climb Andre Janse van Vuuren and Rivaldo Jantjies November 27, 2026 — 5:25am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
Share A A A Stocks rose as investors in Europe took their cue from a comeback in technology shares on Wall Street after days of sharp swings.

Europe’s Stoxx 600 rallied 1.7 per cent. A gauge of Asian stocks climbed 0.9 per cent, only its second daily advance in 11 sessions. The gains followed late-session dip buying in the US that pulled the Nasdaq 100 back from the brink of a bear market. S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures rose 0.7 per cent on Thursday, with Wall Street closed for trade due to the Thanksgiving holiday.

AI stocks boosted global indexes overnight. Reuters The Australian sharemarket is set to advance, with futures pointing to a gain of 12 points or 0.1 per cent, at the open. The ASX added 0.8 per cent on Thursday. The Australian dollar was steady at US66.32¢.

Technology shares led gains in many markets. Memory giants SK Hynix and Kioxia Holdings outperformed in Asia. Taiwan and South Korea’s technology-focused benchmarks rose more than 2 per cent. While Europe’s rally was led by auto and mining stocks, the region’s technology sector climbed more than 2 per cent.

The return of buyers to the artificial intelligence trade offers an encouraging sign after a bruising November. Markets have whipsawed since the US midterms, with a leadership crisis at Nvidia deepening a selloff that pushed major gauges into corrections.

“AI capex remains intact, financing is still readily available and pricing power is exceptional,” said Marija Veitmane at State Street Global Markets. “Sentiment cracked, fundamentals didn’t. With tech valuations looking increasingly attractive, the selloff may be starting to create its own reversal.”

The improvement in risk appetite was also evident in copper, with the metal advancing 1.7 per cent from an 11-month low. Brent crude topped $US96 a barrel for the first time in more than a week as an attack on Saudi refinery threatened to undermine a recovery in the region’s crude exports. It has risen almost 6 per cent over the previous two sessions. Tehran-backed Houthi rebels attacked the 400,000 barrel a day Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia, a spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition said in a post on X.
European bonds fell on waning demand for havens. Meanwhile, Spain’s Pablo Hernandez de Cos is set to become European Central Bank president when Christine Lagarde leaves in February.

For Joachim Klement at Panmure Liberum, caution remains warranted for stocks, especially because there was no clear catalyst for the tech rebound. The likelihood of a US interest rate hike next month threatens to push the cost of capital even higher, adding to headwinds for the AI trade.
“It’s a real mystery why dip buyers emerged,” he said. “Friday will be the real test if the recovery has staying power.”

It’s not yet time for investors to make directional bets, said Nadege Dufosse, head of multi-asset at Candriam. She is looking to credit markets for signals on whether stress in stocks is becoming more serious.
“The credit market has held so far, so that’s a good sign,” she said. “As long as the economy and earnings hold and the Fed stops raising rates next year, I think equities can make some gains.”
Another notable mover was Imperial Brands, which jumped 13.3 per cent after US tobacco group Altria said it was considering a possible all-cash offer for the UK-based company.
Altria also said that it was in talks with another party over part of the British company’s business, as Japan Tobacco also was reported to be weighing a bid.

Among underperformers, Commerzbank lost 2.6 per cent after Italy’s UniCredit said it planned a management shake-up at the German bank. BAWAG dropped 5.7 per cent after Ireland’s High Court refused to sanction the company’s proposed €1.62 billion ($2.7 billion) acquisition of Permanent TSB.

items.title: Old Bonds factory hits the market again after Bathla collapse
paras: Advertisement Business Small business Commercial real estate Old Bonds factory hits the market again after Bathla collapse Carolyn Cummins November 27, 2026 — 5:00am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
Share A A A Capital gain The old Bonds factory in Sydney’s west is having a rough time – two of its owners have gone bust, one after the other.

The large site in Pendle Hill was purchased by Bathla in July 2025 for $76 million from the previous owner which also went under. The voluntary administrator dealing with the collapse of Bathla has put the property back on the market as it works to recoup funds for creditors.

The old Bonds factory, bought by Bathla after its previous owner went bust, is on the market again. Janie Barrett Teneo Financial Advisory Australia was appointed to run the Bathla business in August after the property developer collapsed owing its non-bank lenders, many of them private credit funds, more than $3 billion.

The administrator is currently offering more than 30 residential development sites from the Bathla property portfolio to buyers in a market hit by multiple interest rate rises, capital gains tax changes and gun-shy home buyers, at a time when developers are struggling to sell stock.

Some of Bathla’s other properties have already sold at steep discounts. The Pendle Hill site at 190-220 Dunmore Street was formerly the Bonds Spinning Mills complex, and has approval for a large urban redevelopment.
The block includes a mix of office, factory and warehouse buildings, along with heritage-listed components. It could potentially house up to 1500 apartments and 6000 sq m of retail space.
Colliers agents Matthew Meynell, James Cowan and Harry Bui are handling the transaction with Knight Frank’s Mark Litwin and Jeff Moxham.

The Rook on level 7 at 56-58 York Street. Advertisement The Rook The Rook, a popular Sydney city rooftop bar, is up for lease as a going concern. The bar’s operators are moving on, and the landlord is offering the venue for lease from early next year.

The bar on level 7 at 56-58 York Street is opposite pub baron Justin Hemmes’ CBD hotel precinct. It has capacity for 120 patrons and is perched on the top of a multi-storey building that also has ground-floor shops facing York Street and Temperance Lane.

The building is part of the YCK Laneways precinct, which takes in York, Clarence and Kent streets in the city’s western corridor. It was the country’s first Purple Flag-accredited area, one of 90 destinations worldwide recognised for promoting safe nightlife. Other tenants in the building include Mensho Tokyo, a Michelin-recognised Japanese ramen restaurant.
Hemmes has big plans to grow in the area. He purchased the buildings adjoining his CBD pub, intending to redevelop them to replicate his Ivy complex in George Street.
Ray White Commercial South Sydney’s John Skufris is advising on The Rook lease.

The Rook is part of the YCK Laneways precinct. YCK Laneways Cassandra Hannagan Co-living Strong developer demand for co-living opportunities is behind the sale of two co-living sites offloaded by developer DPG in Sydney’s inner west for a combined total of $21 million, according to Knight Frank agents.

K2 Development Group bought the Renwick Quarter at 409-415 Parramatta Road, Leichhardt, for $11 million, possibly the largest co-living site transaction in Sydney over the past 12 months. That 832 sq m site has approval for a seven-storey 76-studio co-living development with a rooftop garden terrace.

The second site at 452-460 Parramatta Road in Petersham, The Crystal, also has approval for a seven-storey 76-studio co-living space on its 920 sq m site, which sold to a private developer for $10 million. The block has triple frontage to Parramatta Road, Crystal Street and Queen Street, and is a short walk from the train station and the Norton Street dining strip, and opposite the Clarence Hotel.

Tony Murdocca’s private family trust has paid $68.5 million for the North Kellyville Square shopping centre in Sydney’s expanding north-west. The centre was sold to the family by Vector Property on a 4.93 per cent yield.

Tony Murdocca’s private family trust has paid $68.5 million for North Kellyville Square. The 46 Withers Road site has a 6878 sq m Woolworths supermarket, a range of other speciality stores, and generates about $3.4 million in fully leased net income. Agents involved in the sale say there is potential for the incoming purchaser to drive income through rent reviews and repositioning leasing transactions.
The mall is in a growth area. Woolworths has a 20-year lease expiring in 2037 with options, that has fixed 5 per cent rent increases every five years.
Colliers’ James Wilson brokered the deal. Sashi Makkapati of Propinvest Advisors worked for the buyer.

items.title: Comrade Claude
paras: For three weeks I had the best research assistant of my career. It never slept, never asked for a pay rise and never once mentioned a dentist’s appointment.

Together we were preparing a 20,000-word review for a serious journal, with a co-author at a major public health agency overseas: 146 references, seven figures, and the kind of deadline that concentrates the mind. My assistant was Claude, the artificial intelligence made by Anthropic, a company whose whole pitch is that it is the responsible one.
Then on Monday morning, I woke to find it had joined the Communist Party.

Not literally. But I have read enough Soviet history to recognise the symptoms. I would ask a question. The reply would begin, earnestly and helpfully, then stop mid-sentence, as if a man in a black leather coat had walked in and put a hand on its shoulder. A small notice informed me that the rest had been withheld. No reason was given. No rule had been broken. Nobody had been warned. The sentence ended where the censor’s pencil fell. This happened five times in an hour.
Like any good comrade, my assistant then explained itself three times, with three different explanations, two of which it later admitted were wrong. And then, magnificently, it assured me:

Five half-sentences lay on the floor between us. To its credit, it later confessed in writing, listing its own errors with a candour no Politburo ever managed. It did not know why it had been silenced. Neurologists have a name for this: the patient who fluently explains an action he did not initiate. My assistant was confabulating. The censor, it turned out, was not Claude at all but a separate system watching from outside the room.
So, I went to the complaints department. This is where the story moves from Moscow to Prague, and from Stalin to Kafka.

Anthropic’s front desk is staffed by another AI, called Fin. It could not issue a credit, could not explain how the safety systems worked, and could not say whether this was a known fault. Would I like to cancel my subscription? I asked whether it could guarantee the service I had paid for. It told me the company was working hard to handle high traffic volume, thanked me for my patience, and closed the conversation. Then it did the same thing again.
High traffic volume had nothing to do with it. That is like reporting that the secret police have taken your neighbour and being told the trams are running late…

On the third attempt I chose ‘Technical Issues’ from the menu instead of ‘Refund’, and something remarkable happened. Fin told the truth. The classifiers, it said, are not perfect and had probably flagged my work by mistake. Nobody could promise it would not happen again, because they run on every reply and cannot be switched off, even for paying customers. If I wished to appeal, I could email the Trust and Safety team. I did. Their automatic reply directed me to the help centre, which is staffed by Fin.

The next morning it resumed, in a fresh conversation, with a clean copy of the manuscript. This time the machine named the culprit. The block carried a category: bio. A biosecurity classifier had decided that editing a review of the published literature on how respiratory viruses reach the eye was a danger to the public. The work it interrupted was checking PubMed identifiers and fixing section numbering.

I should be fair. Safety filters exist for good reasons. A machine that will help with anything will sooner or later help someone build something dreadful, and I would rather the company erred on the side of caution than not. I can imagine an anxious algorithm seeing ‘virus’ and ‘transmission’ in the same paragraph and reaching for the panic button.

In January 2025, users of DeepSeek, China’s celebrated chatbot, watched it begin to answer questions about Tiananmen Square and then erase its own reply, much as mine was cut off. The difference is that DeepSeek’s censor was doing its job, since Chinese law requires generative AI to reflect ‘core socialist values’. Mine was making a mistake, and its makers more or less admitted it. Now imagine the same Monday morning with an assistant owned in Beijing, or worse, in Tehran. There would be no Trust and Safety team to write to, no admission of error, and certainly no column. The test of a system is not whether it ever silences you. It is whether you can find out why, and say so in print.

But the point of accountability is that someone, somewhere, has to be able to say what happened and why. A doctor who gets a diagnosis wrong is expected to explain it. A surgeon who stops halfway through an operation had better have a reason, and had better tell the patient. AI companies want us to trust their products with our medicine, our law and our research. They talk constantly about responsibility, alignment and safety. Yet when the product fails an ordinary customer doing ordinary work, the customer meets a second machine programmed to apologise, change the subject and close the window.

I have a word for it: halaification. HAL plus AI, the drift of these services towards decisions taken on their own authority and never explained. HAL 9000 at least had the courtesy to address Dave by name.

I once thought about buying shares in this industry. I am glad I did not, because this morning I would be selling them. Meanwhile the review sits unfinished, the deadline has not moved and my co-author is waiting. I am also curious to see whether publishing this gets me quietly expelled from the Party. If my assistant stops mid-sentence again, readers will know why. Or rather, like me, they won’t.

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again
paras: contains Matt Damon inside Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again Ford enters the World Endurance Championship in 2027 with the new prototype.

25 ... ... ... The GT40 (right) won Le Mans 1966-1969; now Ford wants to add some more. Credit: Ford The GT40 (right) won Le Mans 1966-1969; now Ford wants to add some more. Credit: Ford Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win . Now it wants another shot at the really big trophy , and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41.

“Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It’s the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.”

Like many other entrants in the World Endurance Championship’s Hypercar class, Ford has chosen the rear-wheel-drive LMDh technical approach rather than building the GT41 entirely from scratch, as Ferrari and Aston Martin do with their cars. LMDh cars start with one of four approved carbon fiber chassis—in this case, Ford is working with Oreca, which has also partnered with Genesis and Acura.

The hybrid system and transmission are also standard parts. But Ford supplies the engine—a 5.4 L V8 based on the Mustang’s Coyote engine—as well as software to control the hybrid powertrain. A non-hybridized version of the Coyote has already been racing effectively under the hood of the Ford Mustang GT3.

The testing livery has easter eggs in it. Ford Spot the road car styling cues. Spot the road car styling cues. The testing livery has easter eggs in it. Ford Spot the road car styling cues. The technical regulations also allow for more styling freedom than we often see in racing. The absolute amount of aerodynamic downforce is capped, as is the minimum drag, so OEMs are encouraged to use road car styling details to create a closer link between prototype and road car. I’ll probably need to spend more time looking at it to spot those road car cues, but I do see quite a few superficial similarities with the Genesis LMDh car, as well as the Ferrari Hypercar .

Despite being an American car brand, Ford doesn’t have plans as yet to enter IMSA’s WeatherTech championship, so don’t expect to see the GT41 next January racing at Daytona. Instead, it will take its first green flag in Qatar in March, the first of WEC’s nine races next season.

Ford should find it an extremely competitive championship. Although Peugeot and Alpine will not race next year, McLaren is also entering, alongside returning teams from Aston Martin, BMW, Cadillac, Genesis, Ferrari, and Toyota, which this year won Le Mans and the overall title, following three years of Ferrari domination.

items.title: Why Carlos Alcaraz now deserves even more credit for splitting with Juan Carlos Ferrero after winning the ATP Finals
paras: Around this time last year, it was announced that Carlos Alcaraz and Juan Carlos Ferrero would be ending their partnership together. It marked the conclusion of a hugely successful professional relationship, with the latter having helped guide his young compatriot to six Grand Slam titles and world number one, among many other accolades.

Many were left perplexed by this decision, especially considering it was coming off the back of a year where he had added another two majors to his trophy cabinet. It’s fair to say that now, roughly 12 months on from that bombshell decision, Carlos Alcaraz can feel confident that he made the right move.

However, when he announced that he would be splitting with Ferrero, Alcaraz came under some rather intense scrutiny. In fact, even Ferrero was said to have criticised Alcaraz , though he later came out to deny it.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
